title: John the Evangelist (27 December)
hook: the beloved disciple, the eagle, and the one the fourth Gospel places at the cross

segments.voice: Yesterday, Eve, the mother of all the living, remembered on Christmas Eve in some old calendars. Your line was the first parents.

"Lord, who is it?" A question asked at supper on the night before the cross. Jesus has just said that one of the twelve will betray him. Peter wants a name, so he signals to the disciple closest to Jesus, the one leaning against his chest. That disciple leans back and asks. The Gospel gives him no name there, only a description. Today, two days after Christmas, the Church keeps the feast of the man tradition says that description belongs to.
screen: `LORD, WHO IS IT?` → `PETER SIGNALS.` → `A HEAD RESTING AGAINST JESUS.`

segments.voice: Here's the description, in the Douay-Rheims: "Now there was leaning on Jesus' bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved." John's Gospel comes back to it more than once, the disciple whom Jesus loved, and never gives his name. The Church's tradition identifies him with John the apostle, son of Zebedee, and names the fourth Gospel after him. Some modern readers wonder whether he was someone else. The text leaves him unnamed, and that silence may be the point: a disciple known only by being loved. Then the cross. He stands beside the mother of Jesus, and Jesus says to her, "Woman, behold thy son." And to him, "Behold thy mother." From that hour, the Gospel says, he took her into his own home. Catholic tradition reads that as Mary given to every disciple, not only one. On Easter morning he runs to the empty tomb with Peter and gets there first. And at the very end, the Gospel says this is the disciple who bears witness to these things and wrote them down. In Christian art he often has an eagle. Tradition gives each Gospel writer a living creature from the visions of Ezekiel and the Apocalypse, and John gets the eagle, because, the old explanation goes, his Gospel flies high from its first line: In the beginning was the Word. So one man carries two pictures: the eagle soaring, and the head resting on a friend's chest. This week brought Nicholas giving in secret, Juan Diego the littlest son, the holy house of Loreto, Lucy's light, Kanty's coat, and our first parents. It ends here, at the supper table.
screen: `LEANING ON JESUS' BOSOM.` · `A DISCIPLE NAMED ONLY BY LOVE.` · `BEHOLD THY MOTHER.` · `THE EAGLE AND THE RESTING HEAD.`

segments.voice: Lean back against something that can hold you, a high-backed chair, a wall, a pillow, and let your head rest instead of holding itself up. Remember the beloved disciple at that table, close enough to ask a quiet question. If you pray, rest there with Jesus without asking for anything at all; if you don't, simply let the chair and the quiet hold you.
Evangelist. The disciple whom Jesus loved, as tradition identifies him: at the supper, at the cross, at the tomb, and marked in art by the eagle. Today's word.
Your line: the beloved disciple. The Gospel gives him no other name. Day one thousand fifty-seven, done.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the feast of Saint John, apostle and evangelist, on 27 December, inside the Christmas octave; in some places wine is blessed on his day, a custom tied to a story people tell about him.

chat.says: Who was the disciple Jesus loved? Was that John?
options: The Gospel never names him; Church tradition identifies him with John, son of Zebedee.
Yes, the Gospel names him as John every time it mentions the beloved disciple.
No, it was Peter; the Gospel calls him beloved because he led the twelve.
chat.meaning: John's Gospel calls him only the disciple whom Jesus loved; the Church's tradition identifies him with John the apostle.

Douay-Rheims.meaning: the old Catholic English translation of the Bible

Zebedee.meaning: the father of John the apostle

Ezekiel.meaning: a Hebrew prophet whose vision had four living creatures

Apocalypse.meaning: the Book of Revelation, the Bible's last book

The outline hook's 'the only apostle at the cross' was not stated: the text places the beloved disciple at the cross but does not say he was the only apostle there. Index hook line adjusted accordingly; owner may prefer to restore the outline wording.
Identification of the beloved disciple with John son of Zebedee given as the Church's tradition, with 'some modern readers' questioning it. Confirm framing is acceptable for this path.
'Catholics read that moment as Mary being given to every disciple': confirm phrasing.
The eagle: tradition (from Jerome onward) assigns the four living creatures to the evangelists; the reason given ('his Gospel seems to fly so high') is a traditional explanation. Confirm.
